summary: Adıyaman Airport (ADF) is a regional airport in southeastern Turkey serving the city of Adıyaman and the surrounding Şanlıurfa region. It functions as a key gateway for visitors traveling to Mount Nemrut (Nemrut Dağı), a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for its monumental 1st-century BCE royal tomb sanctuary and colossal stone head statues. The airport features a single terminal and runway, handling primarily domestic flights with seasonal increases during the spring and autumn tourism seasons.
faqs:
Q: How far is Adıyaman Airport from the city center?
A: The airport is approximately 20 km northwest of Adıyaman city center, with a typical drive taking around 20-30 minutes depending on traffic.

Q: Which airlines operate flights to Adıyaman Airport?
A: Turkish Airlines and other domestic carriers operate regular scheduled flights, primarily connecting Adıyaman with Istanbul and Ankara.

Q: Is the airport open 24 hours?
A: No, Adıyaman Airport operates during scheduled flight hours only. There are no overnight facilities, so plan arrival outside operating times carefully.

Q: Are there car rental services at the airport?
A: Yes, several local and national car rental companies have counters in the terminal, which is highly recommended for those planning to visit Mount Nemrut and surrounding historical sites.
transport_tips: The most convenient way to reach the city is by taxi or pre-booked private transfer, as public bus service is limited. Havaş airport shuttle buses operate on flight schedules and offer an affordable option into town. Renting a car at the airport is strongly recommended if you plan to visit Mount Nemrut or other archaeological sites in the broader region.
local_tip: Visit the airport café early if you have a morning flight—options inside the terminal are limited and tend to open later than the first departures, so grabbing a tea and breakfast at the small terminal restaurant before security can save you time and money.
